sections.h2: Is a cash sale the fastest way out?
sections.html:
Frequently, yes. With cash, no lender appraisal sits between you and a closing date. A standard listing can still pay off for a home in good shape, but expect to prep the house and sit through showings.

Greenville is the Hunt County seat, roughly sixty miles northeast of Dallas along Interstate 30, so the buyer pool is smaller than in the inner suburbs. Every month a house sits unsold adds taxes, insurance, utilities and lawn care. Set that total against the lower number a cash buyer may offer.

  • Agent listing: fits an updated house and an easygoing timeline.
  • Private sale: fits owners comfortable handling contracts and disclosures.
  • Cash offer: fits an empty house, an estate property or one with postponed repairs.

Greenville was established in 1846, the year the legislature created Hunt County, and incorporated in 1852. Blackland soil made it a cotton market, and railroads arrived between 1880 and 1896. Interstate 30, U.S. highways 380, 69 and 67, and State highways 224, 66 and 34 all pass through, which helps commuters who work toward Dallas.

The 2000 population was 23,960, after a peak near 27,750 in 1990. Local events such as the Hunt County Fair in August and the Cotton Pickin' Arts and Crafts Jubilee in November bring visitors, and a tidy yard during those weeks helps a showing.

Growth came in waves, and each wave left houses behind. Homes near the downtown square date from the cotton boom, and others went up for the workforce at the wartime airfield and the aircraft plants that followed. Plenty of those houses are decades old and may still have their original wiring, plumbing and roofs.

If your property dates from one of those periods, say so to buyers, and ask Hunt CAD for the year-built on its record so your description matches. Receipts for roof, plumbing and electrical work, kept in one folder, give a buyer something solid to read.

sections.h2: Property taxes for a Greenville owner
sections.html:
The Hunt County Appraisal District, known as Hunt CAD, values every parcel of real and business personal property in the county. The county tax assessor-collector mails the bill. On the district's website you can search properties, apply for a homestead exemption and use a truth-in-taxation tool. No one should charge you to file a homestead application, because the district itself charges nothing.

Texas collects no statewide property tax. Instead the county, the city and the school district each apply their own rate to your house, and the appraisal district supplies the January 1 value. Bills go out near October 1, and whatever is unpaid on February 1 turns delinquent and begins accruing penalty and interest.

Thinking of splitting a tract before selling? Ask Hunt CAD about its cutoff dates for splits and combines, because a late request can roll into the next tax year.

  • Protests are usually due May 15, unless your notice arrived late enough to extend the window.
  • If the review board rules against you, the dispute can go on to district court or arbitration.
  • The Hunt County tax office or the district can tell you the current rate for your address.

sections.h2: Exemptions that can lower a bill
sections.html:
More than one applies. School districts must give a homestead exemption, and any taxing unit may layer on a local one. Owners who are older or disabled receive extra relief, and a disabled veteran follows a sliding scale tied to the disability rating.

Texas homestead and disabled veteran exemption amounts
Exemption typeAmount
School district residence homestead$140,000
Age 65 or older, or disabled (school districts)Additional $60,000
Disabled veteran, 10 to 29 percent ratingUp to $5,000
Disabled veteran, 30 to 49 percent ratingUp to $7,500
Disabled veteran, 50 to 69 percent ratingUp to $10,000
Disabled veteran, 70 to 100 percent ratingUp to $12,000

At a 100 percent rating, the whole residence homestead can be exempt. Heirs whose names are not on the recorded deed must prove their interest to qualify, and Hunt CAD runs a page for people who inherited a home.

Greenville's Permits and Inspections Division reviews building permit applications and inspects construction on private property. Permit types include residential construction, pools and accessory buildings, along with electrical, mechanical, plumbing, concrete and energy work. The city takes applications through an online permitting portal.

Built a deck, garage or addition without a permit? Say so to the buyer and ask the city how to bring it into compliance. Open permits sometimes turn up during title work and hold up a closing. Before advertising a house for lodging, ask the planning office about short-term rentals and rental registration, and get an answer instead of guessing there is no rule.

sections.h2: Someone is living in a vacant house
sections.html:
Against some trespassers, Texas offers something faster than eviction court. Under Property Code chapter 24B you may ask the sheriff or constable for removal when all four of these are true:

  • The person stayed after being told to go.
  • The home was closed to the public.
  • No lawsuit is pending between you.
  • The person is neither family nor a current or former tenant.

Removing the wrong person can bring a lawsuit against whoever asked for it. Former tenants must go through justice court. Settle who is living there before you advertise.

A sale is still possible if it closes before the auction. Foreclosure auctions here are held on the first Tuesday of a month, following a notice of sale sent at least 21 days earlier. Once that notice arrives, treat the auction date as a hard deadline.

Closing first pays the lender out of the proceeds and leaves any equity with you. Get a written payoff figure from the servicer, and hand the notice to a cash buyer immediately so the title company can build the schedule around it.

sections.h2: Selling a house with open taxes or liens
sections.html:
Debt on the property will not block a sale, but it gets repaid first. Taxes attach to the parcel as a lien, so any unpaid year is subtracted from your proceeds at the title company, as are a mortgage or equity loan.

Before meeting buyers, make a list with a figure beside each item: loan balances, back taxes, code or permit fees and HOA dues. Judge each offer by what remains once those are cleared, since the headline price says little about your bank balance. A charge that looks wrong deserves a question to the title company before you sign.

Accepting an offer sends the file to a title company. It confirms who owns the house, asks each lender for a payoff letter, checks where your parcel stands on taxes, and drafts the deed and settlement statement.

Signing happens in front of a notary. After the deed is recorded, the title company settles your loans and any tax balance and sends you what is left. Ask what to bring, and agree on a move-out date so the keys change hands cleanly. Cash deals avoid the lender appraisal and underwriting, the usual sources of delay. Before you hand over the house, shut off or transfer utilities as of closing day and leave any manuals, remotes and spare keys for the buyer.

faqs.q: Which office appraises property in Greenville, Texas?
faqs.a: The Hunt County Appraisal District appraises property in Hunt County, which includes Greenville. It also runs the homestead exemption portal and the protest process.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to file a homestead exemption in Hunt County?
faqs.a: No. Hunt CAD charges nothing for a residential homestead application, and owners should ignore any mailer asking for a fee.

faqs.q: When do Greenville protests have to be filed?
faqs.a: By May 15 in most cases, or later if your notice reached you after mid-April.

faqs.q: Will repairs on my Greenville house need city permits?
faqs.a: Most structural, electrical, plumbing and mechanical jobs do. Permits and Inspections reviews applications through the city's online portal.

faqs.q: May I sell a Greenville house the lender has threatened to foreclose on?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale closes before the auction. The auction falls on a first Tuesday, at least 21 days after a notice of sale.
